ingredients.raw: 1 large head of green cabbage, finely grated
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste

steps.text: Combine all ingredients in a large bowl. Cover and chill for at least 1 hour.

name: 4-Ingredient Seed Crackers
author: Carolina Gelen
description:
These gluten-free (and dairy-free) crackers rely on just one type of ingredient — seeds — and each variety has a role to play. Flax seeds act as a binder,  transforming into a glue-like gel once they’re doused in boiling water. The other seeds, like pumpkin, sunflower or hemp hearts, bring texture and flavor to the mix. The seed mixture is baked into a large bark and broken into crackers once toasted. They’re snappy, delicate and so easy to snack on, great for dipping or using as a salad topper. Just like any other foods that are rich in fiber, it’s best to stay hydrated and drink lots of water while snacking on these.
Watch Carolina Gelen make this dish in this video.

ingredients.raw: 2 cups/280 grams mixed raw seeds, such as sunflower, pumpkin and hemp hearts
ingredients.preparation: such as sunflower, pumpkin and hemp hearts

ingredients.raw: 4 tablespoons/50 grams oil, such as extra-virgin olive oil or avocado oil, plus more for greasing
ingredients.preparation: such as extra-virgin olive oil or avocado oil, plus more for greasing

steps.text: Place an oven rack in the center of the oven. Heat the oven to 400 degrees.

To a medium bowl, add the flax seeds, boiling water and a big pinch of salt. Stir and set aside for 2 minutes, until the mixture develops a gloopy, egg white-like consistency. Add the mixed seeds and stir to combine.
Lightly grease a large baking sheet with oil. Line with parchment paper. Using a pastry brush or your fingers, spread 2 tablespoons of oil on the parchment paper in an even layer.
Dollop the seed cracker mixture onto the pan and evenly spread using an offset spatula in a thin, even layer that covers the surface of the pan.

Brush the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil on the seed cracker mixture. Lightly sprinkle flaky salt on top. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the seeds look golden and toasty and the surface is dry to the touch (you’ll continue to bake the crackers in the next step). If the edges start to darken too quickly, tent with aluminum foil.

Open the oven door to release some of the heat and adjust the temperature to 350 degrees. Rotate the pan, close the oven door and continue to bake for 12 to 15 minutes more, until golden brown and brittle to the touch.

Cool to room temperature in the pan. When cool, snap the seed cracker bark into smaller pieces, season with more salt, if you like, and serve (or store in an airtight container in a cool, dry spot for up to 2 weeks).
